data.title: Start
data.content:
You glance down at the pregnancy test you just bought from the dollar store.

You may think that you need to spend more than that to ensure reliability when it comes to such a consequential matter, but...as it turns out, you've come to find that they are every bit as accurate as the ones that cost upwards of $20 at other stores.

You just dipped the absorbent tip into the cup you urinated into less than a minute ago, replacing the plastic cover and setting it down on the edge of the bathtub.

One line means not pregnant.

Two lines means your fears are confirmed.

It's still too soon for any of them to have appeared yet.

You let out a long sigh of dread and anticipation.

data.title: Results
data.content:
You set your phone down for the moment, your eyes darting back to the ominous test on the edge of the tub.

Enough time has passed now, the result is unmistakably clear: positive.

You are very early in the pregnancy. You've only missed one period and can't be more than a few weeks in.

You know that once you tell Marcus, he is going to ask you if the baby is his or not.

What will you tell him?

data.title: Partner in Crime
data.content:
You roll your eyes after reading the text from Marcus. He's your on-and-off again partner in crime, so to speak.

The relationship is quite volatile and unhealthy, but not explicitly violent or dangerous.

You know he's asking half out of a desire to show you support, and half because he would be nearly as displeased as you would to find out you're pregnant.

Thinking more about it now, you wonder why the hell he is even acting like it's that big of a deal to him.

How sure are you that he caused it, if the result is positive?

choices.label: He is the only person I have had sex with
He is one of several possible guys it could have been
I have no fucking idea, honestly

data.title: Monogamy
data.content:
If you are pregnant, Marcus is the only other possible responsible party. You haven't slept with anyone else, so paternity would be certain if you are indeed pregnant.

If the test result is positive, how will it make you feel about Marcus?

choices.label: Violated because the bond is toxic
Smothered because it will make me feel trapped

data.title: Casual Sex
data.content:
Marcus is certainly one possible candidate if you are pregnant, but the two of you break up so often that both of you have slept with other people here and there. 

If the test is positive, how will it make you feel about Marcus?

choices.label: Upset about how unstable the relationship has been
Grateful that you have him to lean on

data.title: Open Relationship
data.content:
You and Marcus have a sexually open relationship, even when things are at their best between the two of you. If you are pregnant, the other person responsible could be him or it could be any of the other guys you've had sex with recently.

If the test is positive, how will it make you feel towards Marcus?

choices.label: Depends on how he handles it

data.title: Dependent
data.content:
Based on your shared history with Marcus and the established behavioral patterns, it truly remains to be seen how you will ultimately end up feeling towards him...

It will mostly depend on his choices and how he reacts to the news.

data.title: Sadness
data.content:
It would be impossible to untangle all of your aggression towards Marcus from all of the sadness you feel about the relationship you have both found yourselfs stuck in together.

You have momentary flashes of anger at him, but the predominant emotion is an intense sadness at how things have all played out.

data.title: Upset
data.content:
You will find it difficult not to place some amount of blame on him for causing the entire situation directly, even if you might know that's unfair intellectually.

Even though you both chose to have unprotected sex, it will be hard not to frame this as something wrong that he did to you, rather than with you.

data.title: Grateful
data.content:
You can admit that the relationship with Marcus is complicated and dysfunctional, to say the least. 

However, if you learn that you are pregnant (as you suspect), then you can't help but feel slightly comforted knowing that you won't have to face it completely on your own.

data.title: Violated
data.content:
Finding out that Marcus had impregnated you right now would feel like a serious violation on his part, however unfair that might actually be.

The way you see things, if he had loved you and truly cared about you, he could have taken precautions to ensure you wouldn't have to go through this.

data.title: Smothered
data.content:
You strongly suspect that if the test result is positive, your feelings towards Marcus may become more irritated, detached or even intolerable.

A pregnancy that you know he had caused would create a sense of being trapped in this current life you are living, and indefinitely tethered to him independent of your own desires.

data.title: Exclusive Truth
data.content: When he asks if the baby is his, you will tell him you are 100% certain that it is.

data.title: Exclusive Lie
data.content: You will pretend to be uncertain to avoid making him aware of his full responsibility in causing the situation.

data.title: Casual Truth
data.content: When he asks if it's his, you will be honest and admit that you can't be sure.

data.title: Casual Lie
data.content: When he asks, you will reassure him that the baby is his, even though you are unsure.

data.title: Open Truth
data.content: When he asks if the baby is his, you will tell him the truth and admit that you truly do not know, nor do you feel certain of how likely it is to be his.

data.title: Open Lie
data.content: When he asks if the baby is his, you will comfort him by saying that you are sure it is, even though that's wildly untrue.

data.content:
Fortunately, the state you live in has considerable laws in place to protect your right to have and access abortion care. 

This means you have several options for how you can end your pregnancy: order pills online (up to x weeks), call a clinic and schedule an in-person surgical procedure, reach out to a reproductive justice organization that specializes in connecting you to the type of resources you need.
